title: Milestone Ownership Roster and Blocker Hypothesis Log
body:
Purpose and usage:
This doc is a working tracker for medium-complexity inference rollouts. Use it during weekly check-ins and as the canonical source for milestone ownership, blocker hypotheses, and immediate mitigation experiments. It is intentionally lightweight so it can be copied into customer folders or attached to QBR slides.

Quick rules:
- Owner is the person accountable for the milestone reaching its target date.
- Blocker hypothesis is a short, testable statement about why progress stopped or is at risk.
- Mitigation experiment is a narrow action with measurable success criteria to validate the hypothesis.
- Confidence is a quick judgment of how likely the milestone is to hit the target date (High/Medium/Low).
- SLA impact is a short descriptor of customer impact if the milestone misses its date.

Milestone roster (list view) - treat as single source of truth for CS <> Eng handoffs:
1) M-01  Production API key enablement for private deployment
   - Target date: 2026-03-18
   - Owner: Samir Patel
   - Status: At risk
   - Confidence: Medium
   - SLA impact: High (blocked customer go-live and invoice schedule)
   - Blocker hypothesis: Customer network team has not completed firewall rule provisioning for control-plane endpoints, preventing onboarding tests.
   - Blocker owner: Customer network lead (cc Priya Nair)
   - Mitigation experiment: Run temporary tunneling test using a pre-approved bastion in customer VPC; success criteria = ability to exchange health check + auth token within 2 hours.
   - Next checkpoint: 2026-03-09

2) M-02  Embedding index import and validation from customer S3
   - Target date: 2026-03-25
   - Owner: Lina Torres
   - Status: On track
   - Confidence: High
   - SLA impact: Medium (affects search relevance but not core API availability)
   - Blocker hypothesis: N/A (validation scripts passed locally but not yet run at scale)
   - Mitigation experiment: Run validation on 10% sample using dedicated importer job; success criteria = <1% schema mismatch and throughput >= 500 records/min
   - Next checkpoint: 2026-03-16

3) M-03  Latency SLO verification under production-like load
   - Target date: 2026-04-02
   - Owner: Jordan Kim
   - Status: At risk
   - Confidence: Low
   - SLA impact: High (latency regressions may require rollback to smaller model variant)
   - Blocker hypothesis: Continuous batching configuration currently misaligned with customer request pattern; tail latency spikes at sequence lengths >512.
   - Blocker owner: Eng-serving-runtime on-call (cc Jordan)
   - Mitigation experiment: Deploy alternative batching config in canary and run 4-hour load test comparing P95/P99; success criteria = P95 < 350ms and P99 < 950ms
   - Next checkpoint: 2026-03-20

4) M-04  Key management (KMS/HSM) integration completed and audited
   - Target date: 2026-03-30
   - Owner: Priya Nair
   - Status: Blocked
   - Confidence: Low
   - SLA impact: Critical (regulatory hold if not completed)
   - Blocker hypothesis: Customer's audit team requires specific HSM certificate chain that our current partner does not present without OOB provisioning.
   - Blocker owner: Security and Compliance (Liz Morgan)
   - Mitigation experiment: Prepare temporary escrow workflow and schedule joint review with customer audit team; success criteria = audit sign-off or explicit list of missing certs within 48 hours
   - Next checkpoint: 2026-03-11

5) M-05  Canary rollout of quantized model variant for cost optimization
   - Target date: 2026-04-10
   - Owner: Avery Chen
   - Status: On track
   - Confidence: Medium
   - SLA impact: Low (cost vs latency tradeoff; fallback available)
   - Blocker hypothesis: Quantization introduces a small quality drift for long prompts beyond 1024 tokens.
   - Blocker owner: Applied ML (cc Samir Patel)
   - Mitigation experiment: Run A/B evaluation on 1k curated prompts; success criteria = quality delta within tolerance band and no >5% increase in human-rated failure cases
   - Next checkpoint: 2026-03-28

6) M-06  Rollout training and runbook acceptance by customer ops team
   - Target date: 2026-03-22
   - Owner: Customer Success Manager (Liaison: Avery Chen)
   - Status: At risk
   - Confidence: Medium
   - SLA impact: Medium (operational mistakes could increase error rate and incident volume)
   - Blocker hypothesis: Training materials are too engineering-heavy; customer ops requests TLDR runbooks and runbook drills.
   - Blocker owner: CSM and Solutions Eng (Lina Torres)
   - Mitigation experiment: Deliver shortened runbook + 60-minute runbook drill; success criteria = customer ops can complete median runbook scenario in <12 minutes
   - Next checkpoint: 2026-03-12

Escalation matrix and SLA thresholds:
- Level 1 (CS owner): first 24 hours triage. Contacts: Samir Patel, Lina Torres.
- Level 2 (Solutions Eng + Eng on-call): escalate if not resolved in 48 hours or SLA impact is High. Contacts: Jordan Kim, Eng-serving-runtime on-call alias.
- Level 3 (Exec escalation): triggers when SLA impact is Critical or unresolved blocker >72 hours. Contacts: Head of Customer Success (Elena Martinez), VP Eng (Ravi Shah).

Risk scoring rubric (applies to each milestone):
- Score 1 (Low): Confidence High, no blockers, low SLA impact
- Score 2 (Medium): Confidence Medium or one minor blocker
- Score 3 (High): Confidence Low and/or blocker with High SLA impact
- Score 4 (Critical): Blocker with Regulatory/Legal SLA impact or customer go-live blocker

How to run the weekly check-in:
- Before the meeting: owners update their milestone row in this doc and paste one-line block summary in Slack thread #cs-rollout-alerts.
- During the meeting: walk only 3 items max — pick the highest risk by risk score, then one on-track item, then one customer-facing item.
- After the meeting: owners post the agreed mitigation experiment, success criteria, and next checkpoint date. Change log the update in the top comment thread.

Appendix: example mitigation experiment template (copy into note)
- Hypothesis (one line):
- Test action (who/what/where/when):
- Success criteria (quantitative):
- Rollback plan (if negative):
- Stakeholders to notify on outcome:

Notes and open questions for leadership:
- Do we require a formal SLA credit clause for this customer if M-01 or M-03 slips beyond 14 days? (Action: Elena to advise legal)
- Can Eng-serving-runtime prioritize a short-term batching tuning slot this week? (Action: Ravi)

File provenance: created as a templated draft for QBR prep. Copy into customer-specific folder and update owners when moving to a customer instance.

End of document.
